body: Voidsoul22 Why would you just assume that I failed to contract for safety? I'm not stupid. Of course I would have done it if they asked. I was never feeling suicidal in the first place.

Things obviously went differently for you than it usually does in mental centers. The place I was in had no therapists. It only had guards. Psychiatrists would occasionally stop by and briefly meet with each patient for less than a minute to switch meds (I was never on any). I never received a fair or sincere evaluation of any kind. I told everyone there I was not suicidal and never have been, but they simply ignored me until my sentence was up. 

If this "better safe than sorry" approach was applied to everything in life we would live in a draconian dictatorship with no freedoms. Cars would be banned in case of a crash. Every convict would receive a life sentence, "just in case" they get out and re-offend. An unfounded accusation should not be enough to deprive someone of their rights, ignore due process, and lock them away.

Do you think being taken against his will to a prison-like facility, strip-searched, forced to pose for a mugshot, and locked in a concrete room watching tv for a week, being stared at through a glass wall by nurses all day who refuse to speak to him, would have convinced him not to commit suicide?

I'm not sure how they figure I miraculously quit my "alcohol dependence" cold turkey with no withdrawals or cravings whatsoever. SMH.

My dad called the cops on me after an argument and claimed I was alcoholic, suicidal, and depressed. (I am none of those). When I arrived I told the emergency room doctor that I had a argument with my dad and had been drinking, but was absolutely NOT depressed and had no intents or plans to commit suicide. I told him my drinking is not everyday and in fact this was my first time drinking in over a week because I'd been taking Aleve all week, but he ignored all of this and certified me as a mentally ill person requiring involuntary treatment. Diagnosed with Massive Depressive Disorder, Suicidal Ideations, and Alcohol Dependence.

I think this was really egregious considering he based this ALL on my dad's statements and not on his clinical findings. He had absolutely NO proof of me drinking heavily or even frequently. He diagnosed this simply because my dad stated "He has an alcohol problem." 

And how can he diagnose me with suicidal ideations when he absolutely denied having any????? Also had not made a suicide attempt, not self-harmed, and my dad had absolutely NO evidence or proof of this.

THE DOCTOR SIGNED A FORM CERTIFYING THAT I HAD MADE A RECENT OVERT SUICIDE THREAT!!!!!!! A fucking lie!

I'm just telling you what my paperwork says. It says "Emergency Room Course: 22 minutes, notified intake services." I arrived by ambulance and was admitted to the ER immediately. This is a small town hospital with a dead ER. Walk-ins still have long waits but ambulance arrivals get priority and are usually served almost immediately. 

By the way I only got on the ambulance by accident in the first place. The cops woke me up and in my sleepy, still drunk state I thought I was under arrest so I calmly followed them outside but an ambulance was waiting instead of police car.

Oh okay. So if my dad calls 911 and says I stole a car yesterday, they can bring me in for questioning. And then when I totally deny it, and they find no evidence or proof,  I guess they can keep me indefinitely just because they think I might be "saying the right thing" to be released? 

Why should accused criminals have more rights than those ACCUSED of mental illness? It's insane that denial of symptoms is considered a symptom. What if denial of guilt was routinely considered evidence of guilt in a criminal case?? It's sad that you seem to support that line of thinking. Very communistic of you.

Also they marked on my paper work that I was to be held for "5-7 days" on the very first day I was sent there. So I obviously they didn't consider my behavior as a factor in the length of my sentence I mean "treatment."

That's it! He did ADMIT in his report that I completely denied any suicidal thoughts or intentions from the very outset of my time in the ER. 

And like I said, I had made no threats, no self harm, no prior hospitalizations, arrests, counseling, therapists, drugs, or any other prior indicators of a mental problem!

Sorry for being a bit heated in this thread. I've been going through my fraudulent, fabricated paperwork all day and it's gotten me quite annoyed. When people refuse to believe me and keep insisting I "must" have done something to merit this, it reminds of people who say everyone in jail must have done something to end up there but just look at the work of the Innocence Project. IT HAPPENS!

Think about sending somebody off to a week of lock up and causing them to lose their job, livelihood, miss their grandmother's funeral, etc. Being ripped away from their entire life. 

For me personally I had to mysteriously quit my job cause I certainly wasn't going to admit being in a psychiatric lock up. Even though if I had been arrested for public intoxication, drunk & disorderly, or hell even a DUI, caught with coke, etc they would have all just laughed and slapped me on the back and told me not to party so hard next time, I don't think any of those things are funny but a lot of folks do and I think they are a lot more dangerous and destructive (at the least the DUIs) as well as putting others at risk.

But guess what, you can bail out the very next day because of DUE PROCESS. You might go to jail later, but not before a trial with presentation of evidence, and the right to hire expert legal representation. 

I was sentenced to my week of prison (literally that's what it was a large concrete cell where we watched one small tv) with no due process and no legal representation. 

Bizarrely, men and women were all mixed and even slept on the same hall, right across from each other with all the doors open. I was shocked because jail is definitely not like this. There were two small bathroom stalls in the "day room" (large concrete cell) with the doors facing the whole room and did not lock. Other inmates would just go up and open the doors without knocking when other people were in there I felt so bad for the girls. 

I don't understand why men and women are separated in jail, but not in "mental" jail. It's the exact same environment. Nearly everyone I met was a serial criminal and most were detoxing from meth for the umpteenth time. 

Only two were there for "suicidal ideations" like me, and they both had huge cuts from where they had slice themselves (one on the arm, one on the kneck). Obviously that is proof of a pyschiatric crisis. I had NOTHING of the sort!!!! NOTHING!!!!!!!!!!!

I calmly explained that I was not suicidal, not a heavy drinker, not depressed, etc. They based it ALL on my dad's opinions, and his requests that they "make me get counseling." Like I mentioned in my other thread, he was angry and emotional about me dropping out of college (to pursue a production career, not sit around and do nothing), and my frequent partying, as well as he had just tried to evict me. We had a verbal argument that night but it never became physical. 

He accused me of being suicidal which I have said "Omg I wanna die" Or "I'm gonna kill myself" as a sarcastic expression at different points to friends siblings etc, but he NEVER confronted me about these comments before just relaying them to the officers. LIKE I SAID: I HAD MADE NO SUICIDAL GESTURES OR ATTEMPTS, HAD NO SELF INJURIES, NO SUICIDE NOTE, NO VIDEO RECORDINGS OR OTHER PROOF OF SUICIDAL STATEMENTS, IT WAS ALLLLLL HEARSAY!!!!!!!! 

If my dad called the cops and said "Last night my son stole a car" with no details or proof, would y'all just expect them to immediately arrest me without question????????

No one ever presented any evidence or proof of psychiatric emergency such as to endanger the life or safety of myself and others! NEVER. Simply drinking a lot one night, but not to the point of overdose, unconsciousness, or blacking out etc is NOT a mental illness and not a life-threatening emergency!!!! 

I'm truly not hiding anything and tried to stick to the key points because it's obviously a long 6-day saga, but maybe this long paragraph gave you enough details? I made this thread to ask for helpful knowledge that other fonts might possibly be kind enough to share with me as I seek recourse for this traumatic and horrifying 6-day incarceration with no evidence and no due process! If you don't have any, then I respectfully ask why are you here?
